candidates.name: Spatial-hedonics-crime
candidates.what_it_holds: Stata + Python codebase estimating a spatial hedonic panel model of short-term-rental (Inside Airbnb-sourced) listing prices in Buenos Aires (CABA) against neighborhood crime rates and socioeconomic controls; >145,000 observations. Cleaned dataset also mirrored on Kaggle (marcodiazzz/buenos-aires-rentals-and-crime) for direct pull. Headline estimate: 1% rise in local crime -> 0.062% drop in STR price.
candidates.why_useful: A genuine academic-style hedonic pricing replication with committed code and a pullable dataset for a LatAm market (gap #7 geography) not in our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel; useful as a methods reference for hedonic/elasticity specification even though the target variable (crime, not bedroom/superhost mix) differs from our exact ask.
candidates.time_coverage: not stated in README excerpt; Inside Airbnb-derived snapshot(s)

candidates.name: Airbnb-in-Vancouver
candidates.what_it_holds: Implementation of the academic paper 'The What, Where, and Why of Airbnb Price Determinants.' Repo carries committed calendar.csv, listings.csv, reviews.csv (Vancouver Inside Airbnb snapshot) plus a Jupyter notebook replicating the paper's price-determinant regressions.
candidates.why_useful: Vancouver is not in our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel; the repo is a direct, code-linked replication of a named academic hedonic-pricing paper, so it doubles as both a new-geography snapshot and a methods reference for structuring bedroom/quality/superhost regressors.
candidates.time_coverage: single Inside Airbnb snapshot, date unstated
candidates.size_hint: one city's listings/calendar/reviews CSVs, unspecified row count
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Partial - same source family (Inside Airbnb) as what we hold, but a city outside our current 13-city panel

candidates.name: airbnb_european_cities
candidates.what_it_holds: Uses a committed 'airbnb_european-cities.csv' (Rome and Berlin per README, but the file name matches the well-known 10-city 'Airbnb Prices in European Cities' Kaggle dataset lineage - Amsterdam/Athens/Barcelona/Berlin/Budapest/Lisbon/London/Paris/Rome/Vienna - which carries cleanliness_rating, guest_satisfaction_overall, host_is_superhost, distance-to-center and room_type fields not present in raw Inside Airbnb scrapes). Repo computes median price by room type, cleanliness-vs-satisfaction correlation, price-vs-distance profile, and an explicit superhost price premium calculation, with both notebook and script versions.
candidates.why_useful: A structured hedonic dataset with pre-computed listing-quality scores (cleanliness, guest satisfaction) and an explicit superhost premium calculation is closer to the theme's exact ask (bedroom/quality/superhost mix decomposition) than raw Inside Airbnb data; worth checking whether the underlying 10-city CSV (likely a static one-time snapshot, not point-in-time) is committed or externally sourced.
candidates.geography: European cities (Rome, Berlin per this repo; likely part of a broader 10-city Kaggle set)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Possibly a subset of a well-known static Kaggle Airbnb-Europe file; not the same as our Inside Airbnb 13-city panel (different cities, has satisfaction/cleanliness fields IA lacks)

notes: This theme's web-search modality hit two structural obstacles: (1) WebSearch reported its shared session budget (200/200) was already exhausted before any query for this scout ran, so zero WebSearch results were obtained; (2) the prescribed DuckDuckGo/Bing fallback via WebFetch largely failed - html.duckduckgo.com and lite.duckduckgo.com returned ECONNREFUSED, and bing.com/google.com/marginalia-search.com either bot-blocked the request or returned generic entity/navigation cards (e.g. Airbnb's own homepage, dictionary definitions of 'price') instead of organic results, even for exact-phrase and site:github.com queries - likely because WebFetch's underlying fetch is not JS-rendering these SPA-style results pages and/or is being served a bot-detection interstitial. `gh search repos` (used per the fallback allowance, run more than the nominal 4-call cap because the search-engine fallback was non-functional) was the only channel that produced real results, until it too hit the shared GitHub API rate limit (5000/hr) near the end of the run. Net effect: coverage here is shallower than a normal web-search sweep would give, and is essentially a keyword-repo-name search rather than a true web crawl - a rerun once the WebSearch budget resets, or with a working SERP-fetch path, would likely surface additional academic replication packages (e.g. on Zenodo/OSF/Dataverse, which gh search repos cannot reach at all) that this pass could not find. Nothing found here is a genuinely new large point-in-time or bedroom/superhost-annotated multi-city panel beyond what CONTEXT.md already holds; the closest candidate (giuseppemaiorano/airbnb_european_cities, pointing at what looks like the standard 10-city 'Airbnb Prices in European Cities' Kaggle file with cleanliness/satisfaction/superhost columns) is worth a follow-up fetch of the underlying CSV/Kaggle page to confirm row count and city list, since a listing-quality-annotated multi-city cross-section (even as a single static snapshot) is closer to this theme's ask than anything else surfaced.
